# Kelvin Okuda: tools

One line per tool. Machine-readable detail: products.json.

- Toilet Paper (App, Standardization): Turns YAML and Markdown into BPMN, flowcharts, RACI matrices, icon pictures, Word documents and decks. No language model inside. toilet-paper/index.html
- Vault Index (MCP server, Knowledge management): Hybrid search over a folder of Markdown notes, for people and for agents. No language model in the index, and nothing leaves the PC. vault-index/index.html
- Capy (App, Productivity): A desktop app where you talk to an AI assistant in your own words, and it builds the report, plan or document in a folder you pick. It brings the team's knowledge into each work chat and acts only after you allow it. capy/index.html
- Team Knowledge Q&A (App, Knowledge management): A knowledge layer for a team: pages, search and answers with their source. Every page has an owner, a class and a link to where it came from. knowledge-qa/index.html
- Team Memory Agent (Agent, Knowledge management): Captures every hour and consolidates by code. A week becomes record only after you approve it. team-memory-agent/index.html

# Skills

- Deck and document builder (Standardization): Plans a deck, a presentation or a branded document with you, then writes the source that Toilet Paper compiles. A deck source becomes an editable .pptx on the company master and one HTML file with the same look; a Markdown source becomes a Word document. It also starts an app page. It asks the format, the brand and the classification first, and writes nothing before you approve the plan.
- Report builder (Standardization): The delivery line for a Power BI report. The idea is a mockup first: the mockup writes the specification and the contract, and a set of gates checks the delivery. What runs today is the audit of the semantic model against a curation checklist (an automated pass, an assisted review, a score per category), and a record of the steps, gates and cost of a delivery.
- Design review (Standardization): Reviews an HTML page against a design system while the page runs in a browser, at 3 screen widths, with WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility checks and a measurement of the brand tokens.
- Project coach (Project delivery): A pocket guide for running projects, anchored in a five-phase project process and the principles of PMBOK 7, pragmatic and not bureaucratic. It prepares a person for the conversation with a human mentor and does not replace it.
- OKR cycle (Project delivery): Runs a whole OKR cycle for a team: drafts and pressure-tests the OKRs, groups them into pillars, assigns owners, balances workload, defines a 75, 100 and 125 achievement-scoring model with weights, and generates executive one-pagers (bilingual HTML to PDF) and an Excel scorecard from a single spec file.
- Fabric app method (Standardization): A method to create, develop and publish an app on Microsoft Fabric Apps with its CLI, in TypeScript: prepare the machine once, create the project with the team's rules, develop with an AI assistant, connect it to the data, review and publish.
- Product coach (Project delivery): A pocket guide for defining what to build, the counterpart of the project coach. It writes a feature spec from a problem, updates a Now, Next, Later roadmap, turns research and feedback into themes and opportunities, and runs brainstorming that diverges and then converges.
